items.title: native: a closure's EXPRESSION body was emitted at the closure TYPE's expectation, so `\|k: i32\| Maybe::Just(k + 1)` (a constructor whose site records `Maybe<any>` and whose payload records nothing) was refused as "a generic type instantiated at `any`"
items.body: Found while building F66's probe. `closure_body` handed the body the expectation the literal arrived under (the closure type), which matched nothing. The body now takes the position's closed return, else the literal's written one (`closure_return_position`, which F67's cast shares). Pin: `native_differential`'s `a_closure_body_takes_the_closures_return_as_its_position_on_both_backends`. The remainder is filed as its own item (a closure handed to a GENERIC callee).

items.title: native: a closure literal handed to a GENERIC callee without a written return — `apply(4, \|k\| Maybe::Just(k * 10))` with `fun apply<T, U>(value: T, f: \|T\| U): U` — is refused ("instantiated at `any`"): the literal's position is the callee's parameter type read UNSUBSTITUTED (`\|T\| U`), so its body has no closed return to build the constructor at
items.body: The remainder of native-46's closure-body fix (6620ad0f). Writing the return (`\|k: i32\|: Maybe<i32> ..`) builds. Rec: render a call argument's expectation under the call's own substitution (`call_substitution`), so a closure argument's position is `\|i32\| Maybe<i32>` at this site. Sizing S–M; native lane.

items.title: native: a variant constructor used as a METHOD RECEIVER with a literal payload — `Maybe::Just(3).and_then(big)`, `Maybe::Just("abc").nest()` — is refused ("instantiated at `any`"); bound to a `let` first it builds
items.body: The constructor's call expression has no `expr_type_ids` record, its literal payload records none either, and a method receiver sets no expectation, so `variant_arguments` has no source. Rec: give a method receiver the position the call already resolved (the impl subject under the call's substitution), or have the analyzer record the receiver's type at the constructor. Sizing S–M; native lane (the analyzer half, if taken, is the solver's).

items.kind: inference (M) — surfaces as a native refusal
items.title: an unannotated `mut found = Maybe::Nothing;` in a GENERIC body, later assigned `found = Maybe::Just(value)`, keeps the binding typed `Maybe<any>`: the JS backend does not care, and natively it is refused ("instantiated at `any`")
items.body: B357's shape at a binding: the nullary initializer leaves the argument open and the later assignment does not close it. `mut found: Maybe<T> = Maybe::Nothing;` builds on both backends (native-46's F66 fixture uses it). Rec: a binding's open argument closes from its assignments, as from its uses. Sizing M; solver.

items.title: `vilan fmt` DECLINES a call through a subscripted closure — `print(adders[2](30));` — "reprinting it would have changed the code at this line"
items.body: Found writing native-46's F48 pin (`native/reassigned_closures.vl` binds the closure to a `let` first). The reprint changes the code, so the formatter's safety net throws it away and the whole file is reported unformatted (CI's `vilan-fmt` leg goes red on it). Sizing S; syntax lane (formatter.rs).

items.title: native: a tuple nested in a tuple printed as a nested array — `print((1, (2, "x")))` was `[ 1, [ 2, 'x' ] ]` natively and `[ 1, 2, 'x' ]` on node (the JS backend stores tuples flat)
items.body: Found with F68's printer work. Each tuple now contributes its elements' slots to the enclosing tuple's array (`Js::js_tuple_slots`); a tuple in a list, a struct field or an enum payload stays its own array, as on the JS backend. Pins: `native/print_layout.vl`, `vilan_rt::inspect`'s `a_tuple_nested_in_a_tuple_is_spliced_in`. Tuples are not `[derive(Json)]`-able, so the JSON twin has no reachable divergence.
